evidence_level_ceiling.text: This lane inspected files at rest only: a read-only git clone, two extracted published npm tarballs, and read-only npm registry metadata queries. Nothing was installed, executed, or initialized. Every conclusion below is therefore at most PACKAGED (present in the published tarball). This lane CANNOT and DOES NOT establish REACHABLE, EFFECTIVE, DURABLE, or GOVERNABLE for any license, attribution, or dependency claim. In particular, whether an optionalDependency or a transitive native binary is actually fetched and materialized on a given platform is an installation-time behavior that only an execution lane can determine.

copyleft_found.label: VERIFIED
copyleft_found.note: These are prebuilt native libvips binaries pulled in by `sharp`, which reaches the tree via the ruvocal/chat-ui fork's dependency on sharp ^0.33.4. Every entry is marked optional:true and dev:false in the lockfile. LGPL is weak copyleft: dynamic linking against an unmodified library does not by itself impose source-disclosure on the calling application, but relinking rights and license/notice delivery obligations do attach to redistribution of the library. This is NOT GPL/AGPL and is NOT a viral risk to Tailered's Apache-2.0 source, but it is the most restrictive license in the closure and should be tracked.

apache_mit_compatibility.label: VERIFIED
apache_mit_compatibility.text: MIT is a permissive license with no copyleft provision, and its only condition is retention of the copyright and permission notices. It is one-way compatible with Apache-2.0: MIT-licensed code can be incorporated into an Apache-2.0-licensed project provided the MIT notice is preserved, and this is a routine, well-established combination. Tailered AI (Apache-2.0) consuming or incorporating Ruflo (MIT) therefore presents no license-conflict problem at the top level, and no GPL or AGPL license was found anywhere in the 888-entry dependency closure examined (see gpl_agpl_summary). The compatibility risk in this engagement is NOT the Apache-2.0/MIT pairing. It is that Ruflo's declared MIT license does not accurately describe what Ruflo actually distributes: 94.87% of the files in the published `ruflo` npm package are a fork of Apache-2.0-licensed Hugging Face chat-ui, whose own README inside the package declares itself MIT while an Apache-2.0 LICENSE sits in the same directory. Apache-2.0 imposes stricter obligations than MIT (sections 4(b) modification notices, 4(c) notice retention, 4(d) NOTICE propagation), and those obligations travel with that code regardless of the MIT label applied on top. Separately, neither published tarball ships a root LICENSE file at all, so a downstream redistributor working from the tarballs cannot satisfy even the MIT notice condition without going back to GitHub. The practical consequence for Tailered is that Ruflo cannot be treated as a clean single-license MIT input: any vendoring or redistribution requires reconstructing the attribution set by hand, because the upstream artifacts do not supply it. All statements here are technical observations about file contents and license texts, not legal advice.

findings.summary: The published `ruflo` npm package declares license MIT, but 499 of its 526 files (94.87%) are a fork of Apache-2.0-licensed huggingface/chat-ui v0.20.0 (Copyright 2018- The Hugging Face team). The fork's own README.md:162-164 states '## License / MIT — same as the parent RuFlo project' while the Apache-2.0 LICENSE file sits in the same directory, and the fork's package.json declares no license field at all. The package-level license declaration materially misdescribes the package contents.
findings.label: VERIFIED
citations: work/extract/ruflo/package/package.json (license: MIT, files: bin/**, src/**, dist/**, README.md, LICENSE)

findings.summary: Neither published tarball ships a root LICENSE file. `ruflo`'s package.json files[] array declares 'LICENSE' but no LICENSE exists in the ruflo/ package directory in the repository, so npm packed nothing for that entry; `@claude-flow/cli`'s files[] array does not list LICENSE at all. Both packages therefore fail the MIT notice-retention condition for their own grant, and a downstream redistributor cannot become compliant from the tarballs alone.
findings.label: VERIFIED
citations: find over work/extract/ruflo/package matched only src/ruvocal/LICENSE
find over work/extract/cli/package matched zero license files
upstream/ruflo-v3.37.0/ruflo/ directory listing contains no LICENSE

findings.summary: No NOTICE file exists anywhere in the Ruflo repository or either published tarball, and the vendored Apache-2.0 subtree carries no modification notices: 0 of 358 files under src/ruvocal/src bear a Hugging Face copyright header or any statement that they were changed, despite the fork being documented as substantially modified. This is a direct gap against Apache-2.0 sections 4(b) and 4(c), and potentially 4(d).
findings.label: VERIFIED
citations: find for LICENSE*/NOTICE*/COPYING* over the repo returned exactly 2 files, both LICENSE, no NOTICE
grep -rl 'Copyright.*Hugging Face' over src/ruvocal matched only LICENSE
grep -ril 'modified from upstream|changes from upstream|modified by ruv|derived from chat-ui' over src/ruvocal matched 0 files

The bundle is their only available provenance, so their contents cannot be independently verified against a registry-published source.

findings.summary: @claude-flow/security@3.0.0-alpha.14 is bundled and redistributed inside the cli tarball (122 files) with NO license field in its package.json and no LICENSE file. Its README carries an MIT shields.io badge (README.md:5) and a '## License / MIT' section (README.md:290-292), but neither is machine-readable, so automated SCA and license scanners will classify a redistributed security-critical component as unlicensed.
findings.label: VERIFIED

findings.summary: LGPL-3.0-or-later is present in the non-development dependency closure: 7 @img/sharp-libvips-* prebuilt native binaries plus @img/sharp-win32-x64 under conjunctive 'Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later'. All are optional:true, dev:false, and reach the tree via the chat-ui fork's sharp ^0.33.4 dependency. This is weak copyleft on a dynamically linked native library, not a viral risk to Tailered's Apache-2.0 source, but it is the most restrictive license in the closure and warrants tracking. No GPL and no AGPL was found anywhere.

findings.summary: The committed root package-lock.json declares version 3.35.0 while package.json at the audited tag declares 3.37.0. The lockfile is stale relative to the tagged release, so any dependency-closure analysis derived from it is an approximation of v3.37.0 rather than an exact record. Additionally, no lockfile ships in either published tarball, so the consumer-side install closure cannot be determined from published artifacts at all.
findings.label: VERIFIED

findings.summary: COUNT CORRECTION to the audit charter. The charter's frozen facts state that @claude-flow/cli has 24 dependencies and 12 optionalDependencies. Independent counting from three sources — the repo package.json, the published tarball package.json, and npm registry metadata — all agree on 21 dependencies and 11 optionalDependencies (plus 2 peerDependencies, 2 devDependencies, 3 bundleDependencies). The charter figures could not be reproduced and are not explained by a peer or dev roll-up (21+2 = 23). The verifiable values are 21 and 11.
findings.label: VERIFIED

findings.summary: FAVORABLE RESULT, recorded explicitly so it is not mistaken for an unexamined area. Zero GPL and zero AGPL licenses appear in the 888-entry root lockfile closure, in either tarball's manifests, or in any of the 50 monorepo package.json files. For a commercial platform this is the desired outcome and no copyleft escalation is warranted on this lane's evidence. The clearance is bounded: it covers the upstream development lockfile (stale at 3.35.0), not the consumer-side install closure, which is UNKNOWN in this lane because no lockfile ships in the tarballs and installation is forbidden here.
